comparison_protocol.source: docs/architecture/ALLOCATOR_PORTING_METHODOLOGY.md, final section ('Comparison protocol -- what may be compared to what')
summary: 1. Absolute figures are tuple-scoped (corpus, window, prompt version+hash, model, allocator version, settled config).
2. Across tuples, only benchmark-relative metrics travel (vs SPY/QQQ/TMFC, lift over baseline), each computed over the run's own window.
3. Every drawdown names its ruler (session-sampled vs daily-marked) on both sides of a comparison.
4. EW is not a measured benchmark -- do not quote $120,427/42.76% as measured.
5. Staleness is computed (via this registry / whats_live.py), not remembered.
6. Noise floors are sample-scoped -- Test 4's floors transfer only to the identical 50-transcript sample.
7. Cross-model comparison requires paired rows (gate_ledger entry 1 had zero paired rows -- confounded, not merely weak).
8. State the minimum detectable effect correctly before calling anything significant -- Test 6's sqrt(5) MDE recipe was not defensible; do not reuse it.
